text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs and Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helweg Petersen signed in Copenhagen an agreement on abolishing visa regulations between Latvia and Denmark and the repatriation of illegal immigrants.

- Parliament adopted a law on restriction of smoking, advertising and the sale of tobacco. Under the law, cigarettes with a tar content over 12 milligrams will not be allowed for import and sale in Latvia. Tobacco adverts have to have at least 10 percent of their space used for warning against smoking.
- The president of the Latvian-German joint venture Thormann, Ivars Birins, was shot as he parked his car.
- The Foreign Ministry said a delegation has been authorised to continue talks with Russia on the land border but refused to say what Latvia's stand will be in the coming negotiations.
- LUKoil President Vagid Alekperov took part in the opening of the company's eighth service station in Riga.
- Parliament set up a committee to draft the second part of Latvia's Constitution which will speak about the rights of individual.
- President Guntis Ulmanis asked parliament to re-consider amendments to the law on land tax which envisage a two-fold increase in the land tax rate at the start of next year.
